statusText: Tail risk remains in the low band at 13% while Stress stays high at 75%. Mapped policy state: EA_ON.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is well below the 25% block threshold, so the difficult environment is expressed through Stress rather than through a path-failure state. The 13:00Z-15:00Z US cash-open window on 28 September is flagged as the narrow danger window for conditional continuation risk.
headline: Orderly Sunday reopen at -0.2% keeps Tail low while generational long-end yields and an unresolved Hormuz standoff hold Stress high
body: Nasdaq-100 futures reopened for the new week near 30,826, about 0.20% below Friday's settlement, with S&P 500 futures 0.21% lower inside a narrow roughly 105-point NQ band. WTI traded near $93.1, about 0.8% firmer, after President Trump rejected Iran's seven-point roadmap to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and explosions were subsequently reported near Qeshm Island. The reaction so far is a contained, two-way repricing in thin Sunday liquidity rather than a gap-and-extend path, so no persistent one-way structure has been observed and Tail stays in the low band. The stress backdrop is nonetheless demanding. The 10-year Treasury yield closed Friday at 5.18%, its highest since 2007, with the 30-year at 5.47%, the highest since 2004, after the Federal Reserve raised its target range to 3.75%-4.00% on 16 September, its first increase since 2023, and signalled the possibility of one further hike this year. Cash indices nevertheless finished the week higher, with the Nasdaq Composite up around 2% on renewed AI enthusiasm, and the VIX closed at 14.87, down 5.1%. That combination of generational long-end yields, a $93 oil complex and subdued implied volatility is a fragile rather than a failing configuration. Latest-session breadth and megacap context from the shared Finviz collector was partial, with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, and it is delayed non-real-time data that cannot establish current index structure; it showed dispersed megacap and semiconductor performance rather than aligned one-way leadership. The week ahead carries a dense catalyst stack outside this forecast horizon: JOLTS and Consumer Confidence on 29 September, ADP together with Core PCE, GDP and Chicago PMI on 30 September at quarter-end, ISM Manufacturing on 1 October and September payrolls on 2 October, where consensus looks for a sharp slowing from the prior month. Within the published 24-hour horizon the narrow 13:00Z-15:00Z US cash-open window on 28 September carries the highest conditional risk, reflecting opening-auction continuation as the structure that has historically preceded mean-reversion failure. It is a conditional checkpoint, not an observed path.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours are fully covered by published Claude assessments. Tail held in a narrow 6%-11% low band throughout, while Stress rose steadily from 52% to 74% across the Saturday and Sunday non-trading window as the long-end yield and oil backdrop was reassessed. Confidence drifted from 76% down to 68% through the quiet overnight hours and then recovered to 79% as fresh weekend reporting arrived. Every hour mapped to EA_ON and green with a normal dominant mode; no historical opinion has been revised.
outlookSummary: The published horizon runs from the 22:00Z Sunday reopen through 21:00Z on 28 September. Tail is held in the low band for most hours and lifts to the 20% WATCH band only for the 13:00Z and 14:00Z US cash-open hours, where opening-auction continuation is the specific unobserved structure of concern. Stress stays in the high band throughout on generational long-end yields, a $93 oil complex, a hiking Fed and an unresolved Hormuz standoff. Confidence sits in the solid band, constrained by thin Sunday price-path evidence and a partial shared-context collection, and improves as US price discovery approaches. Monday's scheduled catalysts are limited to the Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index and a Barkin speech; the high-impact releases of the week fall after this horizon and are held in the events calendar.
